title: nvdisasm 12.6.68 dies with SIGSEGV on a relocation offset outside every section
mutation: first r_offset patched to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0000 in the REL section

differential.12.8.55: exit 1: nvdisasm fatal : Relocation offset outside section size
differential.12.8.90: exit 1: nvdisasm fatal : Relocation offset outside section size
differential.13.0.85: exit 1: nvdisasm warning : Disassembling Std Elf to Old format or Old Elf to Std format

cwe: CWE-125 (candidate: invalid read at a computed address; UAF not shown)
impact: local denial of service of the disassembler; memory corruption not established
open_questions: which function contains 0x40b6be (needs symbols or a byte-diff against 12.6.77)
is the bad pointer derived from r_offset or from the section index
does the same input reach a different failure under ASAN
which bulletin's fix introduced the 12.6.77 guard
notes: Stack (gdb, stripped binary): SIGSEGV at 0x40b6be in `and (%rdx,%rdi,8),%rax` with rdi=0, callers 0x44f7c7 -> 0x45a333 -> 0x420592 -> 0x45a9cd -> 0x4202c2 -> 0x45d836 -> main. No symbols, so the frames are addresses only. The guard appears in 12.6.77 with the message 'Relocaiton offest outside section size' (typo included) and is spelled correctly from 12.8.55: the check was added in that window. That window is also where CVE-2024-0124 was fixed (<=12.6U1 -> 12.6U2), but the assigned CVE is a use-after-free and this crash is an invalid read, so the overlap is a candidate link, not an attribution.
